subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
THE FORMAT READ OFF THE PRINTED CLAUSE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.92.2, lines 33665-33668): `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2)`. FUNCTION and the function-name are UNDERLINED, so both are required key words; the two argument operands are unbracketed and carry no ellipsis, so exactly two arguments, both required, and no repetition (feedback_underlining_not_bracketing — I measured the <u> markup, I did not infer from brackets).

GENERIC HALF — the keyword/name/parenthesised-list shape. Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | ...` and `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. The separator rule is what matters for THIS format: it admits BOTH the bare juxtaposition §15.92.2 itself prints and the §8.3.5 comma separator, and the corpus exercises both spellings (below). TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it arrives through the ordinary functionName/cobolWord slot; hyphens are COBOL-word characters, so the name lexes whole.

PER-FUNCTION HALF — the name, the arity and the edition window — is the catalog row at IntrinsicCatalog#Build (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:310): Add(new("TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ss", "TestFormattedDatetime", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2014)). ⚠ I READ THE IntrinsicSig RECORD DECLARATION (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) to confirm the POSITIONAL meaning of `2, 2` (MinArgs, MaxArgs) and of `2014` (IntroducedIn) instead of counting commas. The grammar's paren group is OPTIONAL, i.e. a superset parse; what actually makes both arguments REQUIRED and forbids a third is BindIntrinsicCore's arity gate — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOL1504", ...)` — so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME` (0 given) and a 3-argument call are both rejected against MinArgs=MaxArgs=2.

RESULT TYPE, since the format's clause head fixes it: §15.92.1 "The type of this function is integer" — the row's IntrinsicType.Integer, and IntrinsicRenderer.cs:334 `case "TestFormattedDatetime": return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DateFn(...), 0)` renders it at SCALE 0, i.e. as an integer.

TESTS: both separator spellings of the printed format are pinned by spec-derived programs. conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD" "9999W526")` — the exact space juxtaposition §15.92.2 prints, which is the harder half and is easy to leave untested; conformance:cases/15.3.3.6.1-Offset-subformats/formatted_datetime and the AssertSpec theory write the §8.3.5 comma form. ⚠ NOT TESTED under this function's name: the arity REJECTIONS. The COBOL1504 gate is generic and catalog-driven (read at IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579) and is exercised elsewhere (tests/conformance/2023/pb24_length_physical_keyword pins it for FUNCTION LENGTH), but no fixture gives TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME one or three arguments.

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (the 2014->2023 change record) carries no occurrence of the name, so the general format is unchanged at 2023; 2014 is the introduction edition the family is gated at, and the landed sibling row AR-15.92.3-2 records the same window. Not derived from the catalog row.
